t: Lesson 5, skills. Your instructor is Patrick Diamitani.
Unlike a prompt that disappears with the chat, a skill sticks.
A skill is a folder with one markdown file inside, a name and a description.
Claude reads the description to decide when to use it.
Then your rules in plain language, no code required.
Skills stay light because they load in layers.
The name and description are always visible.
The full instructions load when your task matches,
and linked files like templates open only if needed.
Start with the skills every team shares.
Brand voice, ideal customer, personas and messaging.
Update one file and every output downstream follows.
Build your own in three steps.
Define one specific task. What would you tell a new hire?
Write the skill or just ask Claude to create a skill for that task.
Then test it, fix what's off and repeat.
Quick recap.
Skills package your know-how, so Claude does it your way every time.
Your mission, ask Claude to create a skill for your most repeated task, then test it twice.
Your know-how is packaged.
Next lesson, connectors.
Plug Claude into your tools.
